strengths: Clearly identifies a concrete, previously underexplored failure mode: user-only indexing misses SSA queries where relevant information resides in assistant turns
Motivates the problem with an established benchmark (LongMemEval) and a specific query category, grounding the claim empirically rather than anecdotally
Proposes a lightweight, training-free solution (fielded max-sim keying) that is practically appealing for production deployment
Explicitly demonstrates the 'zero-harm' property with precise quantitative metrics (Recall@10, NDCG@10), making the contribution verifiable
Provides a clear ablation rationale: explains why concatenation fails (cross-field interference) and why linear mixture fails (non-linear max is necessary), preempting obvious alternative approaches
weaknesses: The introduction covers only a single benchmark (LongMemEval) and one embedding model setup; generalizability to other retrieval architectures or corpora is unaddressed
The 'zero-harm' framing is strong but the SSA improvement (+0.018 Recall@10) is modest in absolute terms; the introduction does not contextualize whether this delta is practically meaningful
No discussion of computational overhead from storing dual embeddings per round, which is a real production concern the authors claim to address
The scope of 'SSA queries' as a category is taken from one benchmark without discussion of how prevalent or representative this query type is in real deployments
The introduction reads as a complete technical summary with numerical results included; it pre-empts the paper body and leaves little suspense or motivation for continued reading

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a highly formulaic three-act structure (problem identification, failure of naive solution, proposed fix) with an unnaturally clean three-bullet contribution list that mirrors typical AI-generated paper introductions. The prose is uniformly precise and hedging-free, lacks any discursive detours or authorial voice, and the transition sentences are textbook smooth. The explicit labeling of the zero-harm property and the tidy symmetry between the three bullets (one per comparison condition) further suggest LLM-assisted drafting.
